rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice when giving a service gratuity.

example.english: We should tip the waiter after dinner.
example.traditional: 食完飯要畀貼士畀侍應。
example.jyutping: sik6 jyun4 faan6 jiu3 bei2 tip3 si2 bei2 si6 jing3

rows.note: Use this for money left for service workers as a gratuity.

example.english: I left a ten-dollar tip for the taxi ride.
example.traditional: 今次搭的士，我畀咗十蚊小費。
example.jyutping: gam1 ci3 daap3 dik1 si2 ngo5 bei2 zo2 sap6 man1 siu2 fai3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose Cantonese noun for practical advice and for useful inside information or a prediction tip.

example.english: This cooking tip is really useful.
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 zyu2 sung3 tip3 si6 hou2 sat6 jung6

rows.note: Use this for the extreme pointed end of an object, such as a pencil or nose.

example.english: The tip of the pencil broke.
example.jyutping: zi1 jyun4 bat1 ge3 zim1 dyun1 dyun6 zo2

rows.note: Use this when something tilts or becomes unbalanced toward one side.

example.english: The table is starting to tip to one side, so quickly straighten it.
example.traditional: 張枱側埋一邊喇，快啲扶正佢。
example.jyutping: zoeng1 toi2 zak1 maai4 jat1 bin1 laa3 faai3 di1 fu4 zing3 keoi5

rows.traditional: 喺 A 頂裝上 B
rows.jyutping: hai2 A deng2 zong1 soeng6 B
rows.note: Use this for fitting a pointed head or cap onto the top of an object.

example.english: Put a cap on the tip of the pencil so it will not poke anyone.
example.traditional: 喺支鉛筆頂裝上個膠帽，就唔會拮親人。
example.jyutping: hai2 zi1 jyun4 bat1 deng2 zong1 soeng6 go3 gaau1 mou6 zau6 m4 wui5 gat1 can1 jan4

rows.note: Use this specifically for a rubbish dump or landfill site.

example.english: This rubbish has to be taken to the landfill tip.
example.traditional: 呢啲垃圾要運去堆填區。
example.jyutping: ni1 di1 laap6 saap3 jiu3 wan6 heoi3 deoi1 tin4 keoi1
